answer: Practically, the chain should score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because gale only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, yarrow is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any quill approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
